facts.text: modelName is the name you use in the autoEmbed index.

The catalog embedding-service-configs.yml is installed next to the mongot binary and already contains two ready-to-use local models pointed at Ollama: bge-m3 at 1024 dimensions and nomic-embed-text at 768 dimensions.
Create a local Atlas deployment.
Create a MongoDB Vector Search index on your data.

Index quantization: scalar cuts vector size 4x and mongot RAM about 3.75x; binary cuts vector size 32x and RAM about 24x (HNSW graph not compressed). MongoDB recommends it for collections over ~100,000 vectors, binary with rescoring for most models, scalar for low-dimension non-QAT models. Query vectors are quantized automatically.

nomic-embed-text is asymmetric: Percona's config sets documentPrefix 'search_document: ' and queryPrefix 'search_query: '. Ollama passes input through unchanged, so omitting prefixes gives no error but degraded retrieval.

mongot autoEmbed can be pointed at Ollama via embeddingProvider OPENAI_COMPATIBLE, providerEndpoint http://localhost:11434/v1/embeddings, modelName nomic-embed-text, outputDimensions 768, empty credentials; catalog file embedding-service-configs.yml (custom via embedding.modelConfigFile, restart mongot). This is Percona's documentation.

MongoDB's official local-RAG tutorial uses Ollama: it pulls nomic-embed-text for embeddings and Mistral 7B as the generator, with the Atlas CLI (v1.14.3+) and a local Atlas deployment. This applies to the .NET, Go and Java variants of the tutorial; the Node.js variant uses mxbai-embed-large-v1 and GPT4All, and the Python variant uses atlas-local-lib-py without the CLI.

Ollama's /api/embed returns L2-normalized (unit-length) vectors and accepts a list in input for batching, so dotProduct (which requires unit-length vectors) is valid with Ollama output; cosine also works.
nomic-embed-text produces 768-dimension vectors, so the index needs type vector, numDimensions 768, path to the embedding field, similarity cosine; a wrong index name returns no results silently.

numDimensions is required and max 8192; binary quantization needs numDimensions to be a multiple of 8; cosine rejects zero-magnitude vectors. Query vectors must have the same dimension and come from the same model as stored vectors, so a model change means re-embedding and reindexing.

Pre-quantized ingestion: embeddings can be stored as BSON binData (float32, int8, int1); int1 supports euclidean only and needs numDimensions multiple of 8; PyMongo 4.10+, Node 6.11+ etc. MongoDB lists nomic-embed-text-v1.5 and mxbai-embed-large-v1 among models that output byte vectors.

db.eurovision.createSearchIndex( "vectorSearchOnLyrics", "vectorSearch", { fields: [ { type: "vector", numDimensions: 768, path: "embedding", similarity: "cosine" } ] } )

Local Atlas deployments are intended for testing only; MongoDB says to deploy a cluster for production. A MongoDB Community or Enterprise cluster with Search and Vector Search installed is the alternative.
The following example uses nomic-embed-text, which produces 768-dimensional vectors in the Percona model catalog.
MongoDB Vector Search Index, With Local Atlas and Ollama

This article discusses implementing vector search in a local MongoDB Atlas setup using Ollama and the Eurovision song lyrics dataset. We populated the database with vectorized data embedded in the documents and created a vector search index for retrieving songs based on semantic similarity.

Follow the Install and configure mongot procedure to set up Percona Search for MongoDB. Configure PSMDB as a replica set, point the search parameters to mongot, and create a user with the searchCoordinator role.
You can use Ollama to generate embeddings locally for Percona Search for MongoDB.
Local Atlas deployments are intended for testing only. For production environments, deploy a cluster.
